query: How do you find yourself again?
why_in_two_sentences: Both competitors are readable, article-form pieces from the same positive-psychology publisher, so no substitution was needed. Ours wins on mechanism, coverage depth, and scenario-specific answers, while the two competitors only out-compose us on a scannable top-of-page summary box and inline research citations for authority.
what_the_winner_does_that_we_dont: Open the article with a boxed three-line summary (competitor's 'Take-Away Trio': one myth line, one fact line, one action line) so a skimmer gets the thesis before scrolling; add an equivalent compact summary block distinct from our prose short-answer paragraph.

Insert an in-page 'This Article Contains' jump-link table of contents listing every H2, so readers can navigate our long page directly to sections like the safety block, the ordinary-week table, or the 8-step protocol.

Attach inline parenthetical citations to named research (e.g. self-determination theory, narrative identity, self-concept-clarity studies) at the claims where we assert mechanism, and add a References section, since both competitors carry sourced authority we currently lack.
Add a scannable bulleted 'signs you might be in an identity shift' checklist as its own section, converting content we only deliver as prose into a fast self-identification list.
Add a short standalone 'risks of staying disconnected' section (competitor 2 lists concrete downstream costs) to give readers a stakes summary we never state in one place.
what_we_do_that_they_dont: Provide a mechanistic model of the blank (two circuits at different speeds, the scan finishing before the preference) rather than framing it only as a normal transition.
Ship a concrete numbered 8-step rebuilding protocol at low stakes (order first, three-second pause, one defended empty hour, track what happened after) instead of five abstract directions.
Include a dedicated 'when this belongs with a professional' safety section covering sustained flatness, self-harm thoughts, and controlled/coercive home situations.

Answer 34 FAQs including scenario-specific queries (after a breakup, after divorce, after children, after trauma, while staying in the relationship, whether it differs for women) that neither competitor covers.
Provide a differential-diagnosis table separating this pattern from indecision, depletion, clinical anhedonia, protective numbness, and genuine easygoingness.
Provide a 'recovered end' table translating the fixed state into concrete ordinary-Wednesday behaviours, giving readers a destination the competitors never picture.

above_the_fold.ours: Reader sees the H1 question, a boxed 'short answer' paragraph, and a list of self-recognition sentences ("I'm easy, whatever works") plus a seminar link; the recognition list earns the next scroll but the answer arrives as a dense paragraph rather than a scannable summary.
above_the_fold.theirs: Competitor 1 shows the H1, a boxed 'Take-Away Trio' (myth line, fact line, one action to try) and a short reassuring opener, so the thesis and one immediate action are visible before any scrolling.
above_the_fold.gap: Add a compact scannable summary block (three to four one-line takeaways) above or beside our prose short-answer, so a skimmer gets the claim-plus-first-action at a glance the way the competitor's boxed trio does.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: Why do I feel lost even when my life looks fine from the outside?
Is losing your sense of self the same as an identity crisis?
What are the risks of staying disconnected from yourself?
trust_signals: Both competitors carry named authors, a 'scientifically reviewed by' credentialed byline, and inline peer-reviewed citations with a References list, whereas ours offers a named author and lived-experience specificity but no external sourcing.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Add a scannable boxed summary of key takeaways at the top plus a jump-link table of contents, so our deeper content becomes skimmable and navigable the way both ranking competitors are.
